research.ask: "homes_by_decade" — the age of {city}'s housing stock, as an object whose keys are exactly "Before 1960", "1960-1979", "1980-1999", "2000-2009", "2010 or later" and whose values are the plain-number PERCENTAGE of homes built in each period, adding to about 100
research.source_ask: "homes_by_decade_source" — the source of those housing figures (e.g. "US Census ACS 2019-2023 5-year estimates")

captions: The largest share of housing in {city}, {SS} was built {peak}, at {peak_value} of the stock. Vapour barriers, house wrap and sealed crawl spaces became standard late; homes built before that manage moisture differently and hold it longer.

In {city}, homes built {peak} make up {peak_value} of the housing. Age matters for mould because it decides what is behind the wall — older insulation, unsealed crawl spaces and decades of small leaks nobody recorded.
{peak} accounts for {peak_value} of {city}'s homes. The older the structure, the more likely a moisture problem has had years to develop out of sight.
